title: Google ForTy Forest Map: 2 Taiwan Pixels, 6 Class Scores
description:
Calculate scores for ForTy's 6 land classes from 2 real pixels in Taiwan; these include OtherLand (other land).
For anyone who wants to understand AI map outputs but has never read remote sensing files: use all the values, the remainder calculation and division to complete a pixel record.

Calculations use Forest Typology 2020 (v1). The early-release 2017–2025 annual series shared in the October 2026 research introduction is treated separately; B is a deliberately selected low-score reading example, not an accuracy sample.

Data: Neumann et al. (2026), Forest Typology 2020 (v1).
DOI: https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/32288616/versions/1
DOI: 10.25452/figshare.plus.32288616.v1
License CC BY 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Adaptations in this video: cropping, remainder calculations, classification using the first maximum, and redrawing. The charts do not use a satellite basemap.

Video data pack (raw values, coordinates and selection rules): https://github.com/x812033727/travel_scanner/tree/e0c70c899/docs/videos/forty-forest-map/data

chapters.first-grid: Read a Green Cell in Taiwan

7732.text: Take 10×10 cells around the target; red marks just the cell we'll calculate.

8aw6.text: I took this green ForTy cell from Taiwan's 2020 data.

gngj.text: The map has 6 classes. Why are only 5 values stored?

ep85.text: What unit is that 248 stored in?

jw6i.text: Another cell is green too. Will it give the same results?

5ur9.text: DeepMind showed ForTy this week. Read these 2 cells.

m2p6.text: Read not just the trees in this green cell, but how they grew and their use.

erqz.text: Primary forest: native tree species, no visible human disturbance.

t4w3.text: Naturally regenerating forest: mostly natural regrowth; secondary included.

66nz.text: Where do forests planted by people fit in this table?

3pse.text: Planted forest is mainly planted or sown; this data requires rotations over 40 years.

v9fh.text: A rotation covers planting, management and reharvest, not a tree's current age.

7id9.text: Plantation forest has more intensive management, often few species, even ages and regular spacing.

2vcb.text: Its rotation criterion is 40 years or less.

yiya.text: Tree crops and agroforestry include oil palm, rubber and orchards for non-timber farm products.

rrgq.text: Lastly, other land may include urban trees or sparse woody plants.

fbc5.text: Each of these 6 classes has a fixed position. Read each value with its name.

gsa7.text: But how can a model tell these differences from satellite images?

9wmz.text: AlphaEarth first turns years of satellite readings into numbers.

jkby.text: ForTy uses them for clues to planting patterns, seasons and growth cycles.

5nt9.text: Training also uses sites labeled by experts and regional data to link clues to land types.

m8cb.text: This green cell stores the model's class scores in 5 integers.

p2ry.text: Find the right 5 values: first check data year and place.

yi97.text: 10 m is the output grid scale, not a list of tree locations.

2k27.text: Keep fixed class names beside values so numbers stay with their class.

vk36.text: The 6 class values total 250. The value 255 is reserved for no data.

gfes.text: Exclude any no-data cell; don't count its marker as a score.

e826.text: 5 values are valid; derive other land's value, then compare 6 classes.

svhy.text: Keep field names with values; numbers alone don't identify a class.

3gwz.text: How do we fill the opening's class-6 gap here?

7iv8.text: Class 6 is 250 minus the other 5 values' sum.

bxdi.text: This cell's 5 values, in order, are 0, 248, 0, 0, 0.

anxa.text: 248 is a stored, scaled score, not a tree count or square meters.

up9r.text: 248 is naturally regenerating forest; the other 4 classes are 0. The sum is 248.

4av2.text: Then check that all 6 values are between 0 and 250, and their sum is 250.

8hpb.text: How do we turn these stored values into model scores from 0 to 1?

ywu9.text: Divide each by 250. For naturally regenerating forest, 248 becomes 0.992.

eym7.text: The other 4 stored values are 0, so their scores are also 0.

k3i2.text: The 6 scores add up to exactly 1.

p9sg.text: This splits one total; it isn't 6 unrelated ratings.

dkq3.text: Of all 6, only naturally regenerating forest scores highest.

w86h.text: Use the top-scoring class; the red-boxed cell turns green.

wh49.text: This is argmax: it chooses a class and doesn't retain all the scores.

6ybg.text: Record naturally regenerating forest as the sole top class, with all 6 scores.

xxju.text: Green gives a class name; values reveal its score distribution.

endc.text: Can we choose as clearly for another cell from the same source?

appe.text: Now another cell in this block, chosen for the lowest maximum score.

beg8.text: Reading practice, not random sampling for overall map accuracy

fe8z.text: The second cell's pixel center is at 121.42234°E.

ymf8.text: 24.69528°N. Use this location to find the red-boxed cell.

mfsh.text: Naturally regenerating forest 86, plantation forest 1, tree crops 77: total 164.

97h6.text: Naturally regenerating forest and other land both have 86, tying for highest.

8mtz.text: Divide both by 250 to get the same score, 0.344.

y64h.text: Primary forest and planted forest are 0.

afyy.text: Before recording the second cell, do these 6 scores also add up to 1?

f2ze.text: Add the 2 scores of 0.344 to get 0.688.

n37p.text: Last, add 0.004 for exactly 1; the other 2 classes' zeros leave it unchanged.

ecb8.text: Wrong sum? Check missed terms and decimal places; match each class name.

8k4a.text: If only one color is shown, which class is chosen?

z33x.text: Showing one class compresses 6 scores into one label; it doesn't break the tie.

wnrz.text: Our map picks the first top-scoring class in class order.

ywz8.text: So it gets the naturally regenerating forest color too.

ww8v.text: Remember the first green cell: just one top class

mx7g.text: Put both side by side: same color, different information.

7qfx.text: Record the tie: naturally regenerating forest and other land; note first-in-order display.

hbci.text: To compare results, read the note; don't let color hide the answer.

sbkg.text: After 2 green cells, can scores directly mean chances of being right?

upmh.text: To use scores, first separate model scores from real accuracy.

vb62.text: These scores lack post-hoc probability calibration.

8m2e.text: To treat scores as chances of being right, use independent reference data; compare scores with real outcomes.

bs4s.text: So you can't directly say this cell has a 99.2% chance of being correct.

ci5j.text: The model sees clues; check land history and management use against reference data.

6ss6.text: Once scores are clear, keep location and data year in the same row.

rume.text: Released in May, the baseline describes land conditions in 2020.

pvkj.text: The formal data paper was published on October 21.

ncx4.text: That introduction also shared an early-release annual series for 2017–2025.

j5kv.text: One location can have yearly outputs, extending classification over time.

nqyj.text: Compare one place: fix location; keep each year's class order and all 6 scores.

wfb2.text: Changing only colors hides the ties and score gaps we just saw.
